name: Idigna
description: A star 35 parsecs away, 1.8 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7535: radius 1.754 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 5.565 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.066) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7535: effective temperature 6699 +/- 216 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.099)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7535: distance 35.088 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.034), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 35 parsecs away, 1.8 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 5.565 times the Sun's luminosity at 6,699 K, so 1.754 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 7535: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Pi Piscium
quotes.card: Pi Piscium, also named Idigna, is a spectroscopic binary star in the zodiac constellation of Pisces.
quotes.introduction: It is faintly visible to the naked eye, having an apparent visual magnitude of 5.60.
